item.title: Weekly Training Net Format Change
item.description: The PACT Weekly Training Net now begins with check-ins on 439.800 MHz simplex before moving to the '47 Repeater for announcements, traffic, and training.
item.content:encoded:
The PACT Weekly Training Net has a new format!

The net will continue to be held every Wednesday at 2030 hrs (8:30 PM), but we will now use a two-part format.

1. Check-Ins​

The net will begin with member check-ins on:

439.800 MHz Simplex

After check-ins are complete, participants will switch to the '47 Repeater for the remainder of the net.

2. Announcements & Training​

The second portion of the net will include announcements, traffic, and a weekly training topic on the '47 Repeater:

'47 Repeater
RX: 444.325 MHz
TX: 449.325 MHz
CTCSS: 100.0 Hz

Members are encouraged to participate each Wednesday to practice radio procedures, stay informed, and build familiarity with PACT communications.

For complete net information and procedures, visit the Weekly Training Net page.

PACT Leadership TeamProvo Auxiliary Communications Team

item.title: PACT Apparel Now Available
item.description: PACT-branded shirts, hats, vests, patches, and other apparel are now available for members to order.
item.content:encoded:
PACT-branded apparel is now available for members to order!

Members can choose from a variety of PACT clothing and gear, including shirts, hats, vests, patches, and other items.

Wearing PACT apparel helps identify team members and promotes a consistent, professional team presence during training, public service events, and emergency operations.

Visit the PACT Clothing page to view available items, ordering information, and current options.

item.title: PACT Is Now On LinkedIn
item.description: Connect with the Provo Auxiliary Communications Team on LinkedIn and add your PACT service to your Volunteer Experience.
item.content:encoded:
PACT is now on LinkedIn!

PACT members can add the Provo Auxiliary Communications Team to the Volunteer Experience section of their LinkedIn profiles. It's a great way to highlight your volunteer service, emergency communications experience, and commitment to community preparedness.

If you serve with PACT, consider adding the team to your profile and following the PACT LinkedIn page for team updates and information.
